content.title: Illinois beats Iowa to advance to Final Four: Live updates and reaction from NCAA Tournament Elite Eight game
content.text: The Illini trailed early but fought off the Hawkeyes to earn a trip to Indianapolis for the Final FourBrad Underwood is headed to the Final Four for the first time as a head coach. Getty Images Elite Eight celebrations are special Getty ImagesThere's nothing like the faces of guys who just won an Elite Eight game. We get four winners. There's more on the table, sure. But reaching the third weekend is a bona fide accomplishment at every single program from the top to the bottom of Division I. It means something. It goes in the history books forever. Whether they realize it or not, every man on that roster is bonded together forever. Fans will remember the name of the last guy on the bench. It’s beautiful. There is more basketball to play, sure. But I always get a little lump in the throat watching teams celebrate doing something so difficult that so few teams get to do every year.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementBoswell punches the ticket Getty ImagesIt’s really cool to see Kylan Boswell be the one to slap the Illinois name on the ceremonial jumbo Final Four bracket line. I covered high schools coming out of the pandemic in Southern California when Boswell helped lead Corona Centennial High School past a Sierra Canyon team featuring top recruits Amari Bailey and Bronny James in the 2021 CIF boys’ basketball championship. Boswell eventually became a five-star prospect and moved out to Arizona to finish his high school at AZ Compass Prep in Chandler, Ariz., eventually committing to Arizona as well. That didn’t end up working out, and Boswell transferred to his home-state school of Illinois in 2024. He never quite lived up to the five-star can’t miss hype but remains a critical defender and playmaker for Illinois, a veteran on-court presence alongside Keaton Wagler. And now he’ll start in the Final Four.Stojakovic huge off the bench Getty ImagesAndrej Stojakovic has adjusted so well to his sixth-man role off Illinois' bench after missing time due to injury this season. Stojakovic needed just 27 minutes to score 17 points, including several clutch drives and layups to keep Illinois close in the first and help the Illini pull away in the second. He also had five rebounds from the guard position, including three offensive rebounds. If Duke wins tomorrow, his matchup with fellow sons of an NBA All-Star, Cayden and Cameron Boozer, will be fun to watch in the Final Four.A word for Bennett Stirtz Getty ImagesBennett Stirtz is another wonderful success story of this new era of college basketball. The point guard followed coach Ben McCollum from Division II Northwest Missouri State to mid-major Drake to high-major Iowa, finding success at every step. He had 24 of Iowa’s 59 points tonight but only three assists, which illustrates both how good he was and how much the rest of his teammates struggled, especially when Stirtz started slowing down a bit in the second half.But still, an excellent end to this tournament run from one of the breakout stars of March Madness.Illinois joyYour browser does not support the video tag.The moment Illinois advanced to its first Final Four since 2005.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementA moment of appreciation for Dee Brown, Deron Williams and Luther Head. Illinois is back to the Final Four, standing on the shoulders of those icons.Illini's size wins out Getty Images Eventually, size won.It felt like we were going to get a classic finish between Illinois and Iowa on Saturday in the Elite Eight, but the tallest team in college basketball figured out how to use its size to its advantage as Illinois pulled away for a 71-59 win to advance to its first Final Four since 2005.The Illini outscored Iowa 40-12 in the paint, out-rebounded Iowa 38-21 and rode star freshman Keaton Wagler and the “Balkan Bloc” — the Illini’s four European contributors — to the win.Wagler on journey to Final FourAfter Brad Underwood called him not only one of the best freshmen in America but one of the best men’s basketball players in America, let’s hear from Keaton Wagler on the TNT Sports broadcast:💬 “It’s been crazy. A lot of ups and downs for sure. Just staying true to it. My teammates, they trust me, the coaches, they trust me. They put the ball in my hands a lot, and I just go out there and make plays.“Everyone pushed me every day. I’m a competitive guy. I hate losing. My goal is to win every game.”Wagler also shouts out Illinois fans to a huge roar from the crowd.Readers' views on Illinois winJacob S.: Great job by the Illini on taking care of an advantageous bracket. Don't know if we're quite good enough to beat Duke/UConn and then the winner of the likely Michigan/Arizona matchup, but I'd be happy to be proven wrong!Michael S.: Badger fan here. LFG Illini! I'm rooting for Illinois vs Michigan/Purdue final. Best conference by far and we deserve it this year.Lionel B.: Congrats, Illinois. Hopefully, Michigan will join you in the Final 4.John B.: Illinois won this game on the glass, strong rebounding. Well played by both teams. Iowa should be good in the future.Joe G.: This is the Andrei gameUpdate on the horn issues in the first half.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementUnderwood on reaching Final FourBrad Underwood has been coaching college basketball for 40 years, a stretch that dates back to the junior college ranks.Here’s the Illinois coach on reaching the Final Four for the first time in his career:💬 “This group’s special. They dealt with a lot of adversity in the first half. We beat a really good Iowa team, who played great. Our resilience was unbelievable. Guys just kept throwing body blows. We just kept hanging in there. Here I am an old JuCo ball coach from Kansas going to the Final Four with a group of guys that I love. I couldn’t be more proud.“I got a loving wife who stayed with me. You’re only as good as the people around you. I’m blessed at home. I was fortunate to be sround great mentors, great coaches. I just bided my time. I found a group that’s magical. We’re living the dream.”Iowa went ice cold after halftimeIowa made just one two-point basket in the second half. The Hawkeyes were 6-of-26 from the floor and 5-of-18 from 3-point range. Conversely, the Illini were 15-of-26 from two-point range. That's the difference in a 71-59 Illinois win. Getty ImagesTo Scott’s point, not enough good things can be said about Keaton Wagler’s performance today.He struggled from beyond the arc, going just 2-for-7 from 3, but still finished with a game-high 25 points on 8-of-17 shooting.He’s one of the best freshman players Illinois basketball has ever had, and he’s the main reason the Illini have reached their first Final Four since before he was born.Wagler made the difference Getty ImagesKeaton Wagler was a difference maker for the Illini all season, and his performance today was truly the difference. Iowa was able to mitigate the rebounding disadvantage but the Hawkeyes had no answer for Wagler.FINAL - Illinois takes down Iowa!Final - Illinois 71, Iowa 59PARTY LIKE IT’S 2005, ILLINI FANS!Illinois is headed back to the Final Four for the first time in 21 years.Meanwhile, an incredible Iowa run comes to its end.Full reaction coming shortly...SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementH2 0:50 - Illinois 69, Iowa 59Tate Sage airballs, Kylan Boswell is fouled and hits both free throws.Illini fans in Houston can taste the Final Four...Make-or-miss game ... Getty Images Illinois has made seven of its last nine shots, while Iowa has missed nine of its last 10. Wagler and Stojakovic are putting out the Hawkeyes fire.H2 1:12 - Illinois 67, Iowa 59Keaton Wagler hits both free throws, and the freshman sensation is up to 23 points tonight.He has Illinois 72 seconds from its first Final Four since before he was born.H2 1:12 - Illinois 65, Iowa 59KEATON WAGLER TO ANDREJ STOJAKOVIC. What a pass and what a finish!Stojakovic then secures the remound off an Iowa miss on the other end, and Cooper Koch commits a foul.Clutch, clutch play from Stojakovic on both ends.
